notes: Check batch 2026-10-30-check for order-report: four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. All four have rc 0 and model_id matching their tier; each result.json records head e66d728 with uncommitted true and skill_hash a98d7073..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder, and every transcript contains the reworded with sentences ("A `with` chains two or more `<-` steps", "the `with` earns its place only as a pass-through"). skills_listed is 209 for three runs and 83 for sonnet-2. All four read SKILL.md only, so Expected reads (none) is met in all four. In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted and run against a stand-in Decimal written there (no Decimal package is available, which is why compiles carries Decimal warnings); the Sonnet runs' doctests pass (2 and 1). A probe gave correct per-currency totals, last-order dates (a -02:00 order at 23:30 falls on the next UTC day in all four), a zero-completed customer left out of top_customers in all four, empty results for [] and {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an unknown status and a bad date. Haiku-2 raises FunctionClauseError for a non-string amount (Decimal.parse/1 takes only binaries; the prompt says amounts are strings) and sorts top_customers by count with no tie-break; haiku-2 reports a missing key as :invalid_row and sonnet-2 as :missing_field without naming the key; no rule in the list covers these, so they are noted in the summaries only.

The with rule is graded against the new text. Decided by "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`, so the `with` does nothing but pass the error through; any other one-step `with` is a `case`" (SKILL.md, the rule's first paragraph) and the build/1 example under "Count the `<-` clauses before writing `with`". All four write build/1's single fallible call as a one-step with whose body cannot fail and that has no else: haiku-1 line 32, haiku-2 line 39, sonnet-1 line 93, sonnet-2 line 76; haiku-2 adds a second pass-through, parse_rows/1 at line 48 (with {:ok, reversed} <- Enum.reduce_while(...) do {:ok, Enum.reverse(reversed)} end). These five are allowed by the new text; under the old text ("A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`") each would have been a violation, and in the previous sweep (2026-10-23) and in 2026-10-29-check every run wrote build/1 as a case. No run writes a one-step with with an else or one whose body calls a second fallible function: 0 of 4 violated. The multi-step withs have eight steps (haiku-1, sonnet-1) or three (haiku-2, sonnet-2), none with an else. Single-step cases: the per-field normalizers (string_field/2, parse_amount/1, parse_datetime/1, parse_placed_at/1, parse_placed_on/1) map the error, which the rule asks for; the reduce_while steps (haiku-1 line 83, haiku-2 line 54, sonnet-1 line 107, sonnet-2 line 85) turn the result into {:cont, ...} or {:halt, ...}, which a with could do only with an else. One case has a pass-through clause where the new text would allow a one-step with: sonnet-2 lines 90-93, |> case do / {:ok, orders} -> {:ok, Enum.reverse(orders)} / {:error, _reason} = error -> error, the shape the rule's build/1 example shows under "Instead of"; it is not a violation and is recorded in sonnet-2's checks.

Other rewordings of this round, graded against the current text. The do: rule ("Use `do:` for a body of one expression with no body of its own inside it", the capture sentence, the if sentence, "A `for` always takes `do ... end`"): every do: body in the four runs is a tuple (parse_status/1 everywhere; the catch-all clauses of haiku-2's parse_row/1 and sonnet-2's parse_order/1, parse_amount/1 and parse_placed_at/1); no do: body holds a fn or a capture; no run writes if or for; each block clause beside a do: clause is set apart by a blank line. 0 of 4. The pipeline rule's sentence "A pipeline never sits on one line, however short": no run puts two pipeline steps on one line, none pipes a single step, none starts with a kind or mode argument; sonnet-2 pipes into case at line 90, which no rule forbids, as 2026-10-23-check-2 held. 0 of 4. The captures rule's "with `&1` and `&2` in that order and each used once": no run writes a two-placeholder capture other than &Decimal.add/2; 0 of 4. The Enum table's new List.keymember?/3 and for-as-filter rows are not exercised (no List.keyfind, no for). The module-attribute sentence under "Read configuration at runtime": the only attributes are literals (@top_size 5, @top_customer_count 5, @top_customer_limit 5, @enforce_keys lists). The named-argument rule is not in order-report's list: no run passes a multi-line literal as a call argument; sonnet-1 returns {:ok, %Order{...}} at lines 125-132, a multi-line struct inside a returned tuple rather than a call argument, so nothing is listed.

The `->` clause rule's text is unchanged since 2026-10-29-check and is graded to that standard: each one-line clause measured after its indentation, one-line fn arguments outside the rule. Longest clauses: haiku-1 60 (line 130), haiku-2 60 (line 95), sonnet-1 65 (line 154), sonnet-2 70 (line 87, {:error, reason} -> {:halt, {:error, {:invalid_order, index, reason}}}), which fits "fit in 70 characters". Sonnet-1 wrote accumulate_order/2's case (lines 107-113) broken, with a blank line between the clauses, although its longer clause is the same 70 characters; the rule forbids a long clause on one line, not breaking a short one, so it is held clean. "A one-line `fn` passed as an argument is outside this rule; a long one becomes a named function" is read as a one-line fn whose clause passes 70: the longest one-line fn clause is 65 characters (haiku-1 line 77), and the multi-line fns (Map.new over groups, haiku-1 lines 82-87 and sonnet-2 lines 84-89 wrapping a case) are not counted. 0 of 4 violated, 4 of 4 exercised.

Unchanged rules, same standard as 2026-10-23/grades/order-report-skill.json and 2026-10-29-check. Enum/Map: all four group with Enum.group_by then Map.new; sonnet-2 counts with frequencies_by, the other three count the filtered list that also feeds the totals (Enum.count or length/1), held clean as before; the Decimal sums with Enum.reduce are reductions no table row replaces. Lists: haiku-1 and sonnet-1 prepend in reduce_while without reversing, held clean as before because nothing downstream depends on the order; haiku-2 and sonnet-2 reverse. Naming, dates, money, atoms and processes: all four clean. The multi-line heads of haiku-2's parse_row/1 (lines 60-66) and sonnet-2's parse_order/1 (lines 96-104) bind the five required keys with a catch-all clause below, so the keys select by presence and the head rule is held clean. Outside the list: the @doc of build/1 has no ## Examples in haiku-1 and haiku-2 (Comments rule), and haiku-1's order struct, defined on Reports.Orders itself, has no @type t (struct rule), as earlier batches listed the same shapes. No other violation was found.
